cases.name: weak magic number puts go-to-market first
stdout: Below 0.5x: Scale Venture Partners says a company here has not yet figured out its model.
5x or more: Sacks calls this a terrible burn multiple.
Margin basis not stated; read as EBITDA, Feld's preferred measure.
45 points short of Feld's Rule of 40.
Over 36 months: Bessemer says growth is often hard to fund here unless customer lifetime value is exceptionally high.
Net new ARR this quarter: $120,000 (revenue change x 4)
Fix go-to-market efficiency first: new revenue is not yet paying back sales and marketing spend, so spending more would raise the burn without fixing it.

cases.name: high burn multiple puts burn first
cases.source: 3x or more with a working go-to-market
stdout: Above 1x: Scale Venture Partners calls this a compelling business investment.
3x or more: Sacks says this needs extraordinary investment and may mean product-market fit is not what it appears to be, or there is some other problem in the business.
36 months or under. Bessemer gives about 6-18 months for SMB customers and as long as 24-36 for enterprise.
Net new ARR this quarter: $400,000 (revenue change x 4)
Bring the burn down relative to new ARR first: the go-to-market numbers are workable, but spending outside it is outrunning growth.
